caption: : Avg. performance across 11 datasets (y-axis) consistently improves as the number of training examples increases (x-axis). Max is 29k examples, the full size of our dataset.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how “Average Performance” varies with the number of training examples, showing a single series of average results across multiple training-set sizes. The x-axis is labeled “# of training dataset (k)” and uses a linear scale, spanning roughly from 5 to 30 (in thousands), with regularly spaced tick labels at 5-unit intervals (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). The y-axis is labeled “Average Performance” on a linear scale, ranging approximately from 47 to 56, with tick labels shown every 2 units (48, 50, 52, 54, 56). A single black solid line with filled circular markers connects four points and increases across the x-axis: it starts near 47.5 at 5k, rises to about 50.2 at 10k, increases to about 52.6 at 20k, and ends near 56.1 at approximately 29–30k, with no intermediate dips between the plotted points.
